new.notes: PROXY: P150 (400G), not the Galaxy. v4rxv2i3, 2D 1-hop E/W write 1024 B (BndEW1024), 116.4 cycles/packet. On the Galaxy the same build runs this row at 122.9 (Sls1HopEW 1024 B, 4352 B slots, Slurm 167648; v4trm 124.2 against main 224.1, Slurm 163369), so the rate, and possibly the split, differ. Router-bound on both links: 1024 B takes ~34 cycles on the 400G wire and ~68 on 200G (wire model, wire.json).

new.notes: v4rxv2i3, PcsMcast = the census MeshMulticast write row (all-to-all, 4352 B, one link) run longer. Every router carries traffic; the routers are picked by the rule (A/B-named, else busiest).

PROXY, a diagnostic build: P150 3-hop E/W write 4352 B (PcsEW3Hop) on v4rxg3ml, the receiver lead v4rxg3 with an E/W forwarder forced into the N/S routers' shape (stateless forward plus multi-downstream bookkeeping; V4_NS_FLOOR §2, V4_ROUTE_PRELOAD §8.2), 179.7 cycles/packet. Not a production build or row. Routers picked by the rule (busiest): V4_ROUTE_PRELOAD §8.2 sampled chip 2 channel 4's E1, the West-facing forwarder with two downstreams, which is within one point of the busiest. The Galaxy N/S rows are E1-bound by A/B (V4_NS_FLOOR §1); the proxy's bound side is not measured. The Galaxy row itself (GlxMesh7HopNS 1024 B) runs 186.0 on v4rxv2i3 with the default 4352 B slots and 172-173 with 2 KiB slots (the floor V4_NS_FLOOR §1 names); main 222.9 (Slurm 163369).

missing_notes.main: No samples of main's router exist at any of the five points: the only main samples (pcse_v1, a09u32 job 131) are one-ERISC ring 1-hop bidirectional 1024 B, used here only to validate main's map.
missing_notes.5: No samples of either router on a full-ring multicast (Galaxy or P150, two ERISCs). The nearest existing new-router samples (ring 1-hop write, job 358) are a different traffic pattern and are not used.

router_rule: Per ERISC: the router whose ERISC sets the test's rate where an A/B has identified that router (ab_targets in a point or entry, with its source); otherwise the busiest (largest share of samples in that ERISC's work category: E0 Ethernet send, E1 NoC commands). The one-side delay A/Bs (slack.json, V4_BOUNDS §1, V4_NS_FLOOR §1) spin every router's E0 or every router's E1 at once: they name the bound side, not a router, so today every pick is 'busiest' (user, 2026-11-02).
